To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a multi cell MMSE can significantly improve the sum spectral efficiency over the single cell MMSE in massive MIMO systems with pilot reuse, and that the performance can be accurately predicted using a new deterministic equivalent.

a multi cell MMSE can significantly improve spectral efficiency over the conventional single MMSE and the recently proposed multi cell ZF for massive MIMO, especially in networks with a large number of users per cell and/or a small number of pilot sequences.

the new multi cell MMSe detector can achieve a significantly higher sum spectral efficiency than the conventional single cell Mmse and the recently proposed multi cell ZF detectors, especially in the case of large K and/or b, and that the deterministic equivalent of the uplink sum SINR is very accurate even for small system dimensions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
massive MIMO systems, which is a key technology for 5G wireless communications.
a multi cell MIMO system, where a large number of base stations and mobile stations are deployed in a network.
the design of massive MIMO systems, which are a promising technology for future wireless networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed multi cell MIMO detector is a very promising solution for massive MIMO, especially when the network is large and/or the pilot reuse factor is high.
the proposed detector is a good choice for a massive MIMO system with a large number of users, where it is desirable to reuse a small number of orthogonal pilot sequences.
the multi cell MMSe detector is a very powerful detector that is easy to implement and has the potential of achieving a significant spectral efficiency gain over conventional detectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have derived the deterministic equivalent expression of uplink SINR in a multi cell MIMO system.
the multi cell MMSe detector is an attractive candidate for massive MIMO uplink systems, and the deterministic equivalent provides a very accurate performance prediction for such systems.

we have proposed a new multi cell detector, and derived a deterministic equivalent for the SINR, which is easy to evaluate and accounts for power allocation, imperfect channel estimation, and pilot allocation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for massive MIMO networks, a large number of channel directions can be estimated locally by the base station, so the base station can actively suppress the interference from other cells, and this leads to significant sum spectral efficiency improvements.
by using a large number of antennas and pilot sequences, the inter cell interference can be effectively suppressed, so that multi cell MMSE becomes a viable option for massive MIMO uplink systems.
the multi cell MMSe can provide significant gains in massive MIMO systems and the large system analysis can be useful for system design.
